title: Following the decomposition of compound X
body: A student studied the decomposition of a compound X in aqueous solution at 310 K. Samples were withdrawn at intervals and the concentration of X was measured: at t = 0 min, [X] = 0.080 mol L⁻¹; at t = 10 min, [X] = 0.040 mol L⁻¹; at t = 20 min, [X] = 0.020 mol L⁻¹; at t = 30 min, [X] = 0.010 mol L⁻¹. The student then plotted the data in different ways to find which plot gives a straight line, and used it to find the order of the reaction and its rate constant.

title: Activation energy from an Arrhenius plot
body: To study how temperature affects the rate of a gas-phase decomposition, a student measured its rate constant k at five temperatures between 500 K and 600 K. Using the Arrhenius equation in logarithmic form, ln k = −Ea/RT + ln A, the student plotted ln k (k in s⁻¹) against 1/T (in K⁻¹). The points lay on a straight line with a slope of −1.2 × 10⁴ K. The student noted that a steeper (more negative) slope would mean a reaction whose rate is more sensitive to temperature.
